title: SUP.9 Problem resolution management: populated process record for Project Northcell

standards_mappings.rationale: Problem resolution management: intake, classification, investigation, disposition and trend.
standards_mappings.relationship_note: The rationale states the derivation explicitly ('problem resolution management'): this record was written from the clause's concept, or supplies the work product the clause expects, or consumes the one the clause produces. The clause is the intellectual source of the content, which is what `derivation_basis` names. It is NOT a conformance claim: no clause text was consulted, no assessment was performed, and the clause is not a yardstick this record was measured against.

lifecycle_status_note: Set to the value above because no human has reviewed or approved this record. `automated_review_status` below refers to corpus automation (schema, link, provenance and consistency checks run by docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py) and is not a statement about engineering validity, organisational independence or human confirmation.

revision_history.author: quality_engineer
revision_history.description: Supporting-process record authored because the generated view reported SUP.9 as a coverage gap: no record whose engineering_domain is 'supporting' named the process. This record populates it - definition, inputs, outputs, accountable role, acceptance criteria, at least one performed instance with fictional participants and a synthetic decision, and the communication records showing how agreed revisions reach affected roles.

fictional_organisation.name: Halden Cell Systems (fictional) problem resolution board (fictional)

purpose: Ensure that every defect found in the corpus is recorded, classified, assigned, worked to a disposition and closed only on evidence, and that the trend across problems is visible.
definition: A problem in this corpus is either a review finding, a validator finding or a governance inconsistency. Each becomes a finding record with a severity, a category, evidence, an impact, a root cause, a resolution and a disposition. Closure requires the resolution field to state what was actually done, which means that a finding whose resolution reads 'not resolved' stays open and visible.

inputs.input: Findings raised by the corpus validator
Inconsistencies found while reading records against each other

outputs.output: A finding record per problem, carrying all seven required fields
A disposition per finding, including the decision not to work it
A severity trend across the programme
outputs.retention: for the programme duration plus the trend window

accountable_role.independence: The problem resolution board may not close a problem the author of the affected record raised. That separation is structural in this corpus and is not tested by any check.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Every finding carries all seven required fields
acceptance_criteria.evidence_of_conformance: 28 finding records validate. Making the fields mandatory in the schema is what makes this criterion checkable at all.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A finding whose resolution is 'not resolved' carries disposition accepted or deferred rather than closed
acceptance_criteria.how_conformance_is_checked: Read the resolution and disposition fields together and confirm the pair is coherent.
acceptance_criteria.evidence_of_conformance: FB2-REV-FND-000008 through FB2-REV-FND-000012 each state 'NOT RESOLVED' and carry disposition 'accepted'. The pairing rule is what lets an open problem be visible rather than hidden behind a closed disposition.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: No problem is closed by editing the record it was raised against
acceptance_criteria.how_conformance_is_checked: Compare the affected record's revision against the revision it had when the finding was raised.
acceptance_criteria.evidence_of_conformance: Six findings raised in this pass name records at revision 1 and those records are still at revision 1. The contradictions are recorded rather than corrected.

performed_instances.instance_description: Intake and disposition of the six contradictions found while writing the technical safety concept, plus the five pre-existing findings against the security requirements.

participants.named_as: role identity: quality_engineer (intake and classification, fictional)
role identity: safety_engineer (author of two of the affected records, fictional)
role identity: hw_engineer (author of one of the affected records, fictional)

performed_instances.decision_or_outcome: Six problems accepted and recorded against the pre-existing records. Five pre-existing problems accepted against the security requirements remain open on the point that they have no verification evidence: the measures that would close them are now authored but unexecuted, so the evidence still does not exist and the findings still stand.
non_conformances_found: Criterion 3 cannot be verified for the whole corpus: no revision-history audit tool exists, so the criterion is asserted from the reviewer's own record of what was and was not edited rather than demonstrated by a check. Asserting a control without a mechanism to verify it is a weakness of the process, recorded here rather than hidden.

process_performance_measurement.how_measured: Count instances judged conforming against the process's own acceptance criteria, over the number of instances. 'partially_conforming' counts as not conforming.

limitations: Synthetic process record for a synthetic project.

The five findings against the security requirements are recorded as resolved in neither direction: the measures now exist, the executions are blocked, and the requirement therefore still has no verification evidence. Recording the measures as closing the finding would be the single most convenient dishonesty available in this pass and it was not taken.
The trend this process is supposed to produce cannot be produced from a corpus of one intake cycle. No trend line is drawn from a single cycle and none is claimed.
